$comment: Every agent ai_tooling/setup.ps1 sets up, and where each one wants things. setup.ps1,
verify-agent-setup.ps1 and the delivery table in ai_tooling/documentation/overview.md all read this
file; none of them holds an agent's paths of its own. Adding an agent means adding
an entry here (and a writer in ai_tooling/lib/AgentSetup.psm1 if it needs a new rule format).
The order of the entries is the order of the interactive prompt and of -Agent all.
Paths are relative to the repository root, or to the home folder where mcp.root
(for mcp.legacyFiles: mcp.legacyRoot) is 'home', with forward slashes.
What setup publishes follows from three facts per agent (documentation/agent-setup.md):
skillLinks           'junction' or 'copy': how each published skill gets into
its skills folder. Copies for agents that do not follow
resolvesImports      follows '@file' lines in its instruction files. If not,
PERMISSIONS.md and ai_tooling/instructions/ are copied into its
readsNestedAgentsMd  reads an app folder's AGENTS.md by itself. If not, and no
importing stub in the app folder brings it in, each app's
AGENTS.md is copied as a rule scoped to that app.

claude.name: Claude Code

detect.$why: The JetBrains plugin ships no CLI of its own and refuses to start unless 'claude' is on PATH.

claude.$skillLinks: Tested 2026-10-06: a junction per skill in .claude/skills is listed at session start. Skills in a group folder below it are not; .claude/skills in an app folder only once a file in that app is read.
claude.$disableModelInvocation: Command-only skills (disable-model-invocation: true) are kept out of the agent's skill list, as documented (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills). Seen 2026-10-15 in a Claude Code session of the desktop app (2.1.295 installed): a command-only project skill, grill-me, grill-with-docs, ask-matt, handoff, retro and teach were missing from the session's skill list, grilling was there. Typing /name was not tried in that check.
claude.$subagents: The definitions in ai_tooling/agents/. Only Claude Code reads subagent definitions; for the other agents the rule that dispatches a subagent says what to do instead.
claude.$stub: The app stub brings the app's AGENTS.md in once a file in that app is read: tested 2026-10-21 with the desktop app 3.1623.0 and the extension 2.1.306 in Antigravity IDE 2.5.5 (documentation/agent-setup.md, 'When app rules load').
claude.$resolvesImports: Tested 2026-10-05: plain '@file' lines, '[@file](file)', nested imports, and '@../' from an app AGENTS.md once a file in that app is read.
claude.$personal: Checked 2026-10-12 against https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp. A personal skill beats a project skill of the same name ("personal over project"). An MCP server of the local scope, stored in ~/.claude.json under projects.{project path}.mcpServers, beats the project's .mcp.json; the user scope (top-level mcpServers there) loses to it and is not read.

gemini.name: Gemini / Antigravity

detect.$why: Checked 2026-10-19 on a machine with Antigravity 2.1.4 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5: their install of 2026-06-22 created .gemini/antigravity-ide and, 41 s later, .gemini/config (with a .migrated marker); Gemini CLI, used on the same machine, wrote neither. Not .gemini/config: setup creates that folder itself when it writes the MCP config there (mcp.keepValid), so it would detect its own output. A fresh install on a clean machine was not tried.

gemini.$skillLinks: Tested 2026-10-06 with Antigravity: a junction per skill in .agents/skills is not listed, while a junction that is the whole folder is. So each skill is copied. Skills in an app folder are not listed.
gemini.$disableModelInvocation: Not tested (2026-10-15): no chat was run. Antigravity's skills docs (https://antigravity.google/docs/skills) name only name and description. The language servers of Antigravity IDE 2.5.5 and Antigravity 2.1.4 contain a 'disable-model-invocation' YAML field, so they read it; whether they then keep the skill out of the agent's list is unknown. Gemini CLI's skill loader reads only name and description (google-gemini/gemini-cli, packages/core/src/skills/skillLoader.ts on main), so Gemini CLI does not honour it. Probe: documentation/agent-setup.md, 'Command-only skills'.
gemini.$stub: The app stubs do nothing for Antigravity (tested); kept for Gemini CLI, which reads nested GEMINI.md files.
gemini.$resolvesImports: Tested 2026-10-05 with Antigravity 2.5.5: it saw the text of the root AGENTS.md, but none of the files it imports, in any form.
gemini.$readsNestedAgentsMd: Tested the same day: an app folder's AGENTS.md did not load, not even after reading a file in that folder.
gemini.$rules: The app rules, and an instruction file whose own frontmatter says trigger: glob or has no trigger, are written as trigger: model_decision, the globs named in the description; an instruction file with another trigger goes as it is. Tested 2026-10-21 with Antigravity 2.24.0 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5: a rule without trigger was not listed under Customizations and never loaded, at the start, on a read, an edit or a question matching its description. Tested 2026-10-21 with Antigravity 2.24.0 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5: a trigger: glob rule never loaded, on a read, an edit or with the file open in the editor; a model_decision rule was read by the model before an edit in its folder, also without being told to follow project rules (documentation/agent-setup.md, 'When app rules load').

mcp.$httpUrlField: Tested 2026-10-13 with Antigravity IDE 2.5.5: a server with httpUrl failed to load ('no connector can handle spec'); the IDE's bundled mcp_config.schema.json knows only serverUrl for a remote server.
mcp.$why: The workspace file, one per clone (https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp: 'Configured in your active project under .agents/mcp_config.json'; the docs bundled with Antigravity IDE 2.5.5 name only the global ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json and plugin configs). Tested 2026-10-20 with Antigravity 2.24.0 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5, both opened on the repository root: a probe server only in .agents/mcp_config.json was listed and started (the IDE started it after the global ones), one only in the global file too, and a server of the same name in both ran the global one. So the global file wins on a name clash: setup never writes the project's servers there, and verify-agent-setup.ps1 warns about a server in it named like a project one.
mcp.$legacyRoot: The root of keepValid (and of legacyFiles, files an earlier setup version wrote and later runs take the project's servers out of; none in this project yet).
mcp.$keepValid: Tested 2026-10-20 with Antigravity 2.24.0: after setup deleted the global file, Antigravity recreated it empty (0 bytes) and then loaded no MCP server at all, not even the workspace file's; with { "mcpServers": {} } in it, Antigravity 2.24.0 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5 loaded the workspace file's servers. A fresh install may create the file empty too. So setup writes an empty server list into a missing or empty one and never deletes it. A bare {} works too: tested 2026-10-20 with Antigravity 2.24.0 and Antigravity IDE 2.5.5, the four workspace servers loaded.

gemini.$personal: Checked 2026-10-12 against https://antigravity.google/docs/skills. Personal skills: ~/.gemini/config/skills, the legacy ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills, and ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills for Antigravity CLI. Which one wins for the same name is not documented. Personal MCP servers: the global ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, which wins over the workspace file on a name clash (mcp.$why above).

copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
copilot.$skillLinks: Tested 2026-10-06: a junction per skill is listed. Copilot also reads .claude/skills and .agents/skills; a name found in several of them is listed once, and the copy in .agents/skills wins. Skills in an app folder are not listed.
copilot.$disableModelInvocation: Honours it, going by the installed code, not a chat run (2026-10-15, VS Code 1.140.0 with its built-in Copilot Chat 0.68.0): both places that build the skill list for the system prompt, in VS Code and in the extension, leave out a skill with disable-model-invocation: true, and user-invocable defaults to true, so it stays a / command. Documented since VS Code 1.109 (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/agent-skills).
copilot.$resolvesImports: Not tested: Copilot's documentation describes no import syntax, so '@file' is plain text.
copilot.$readsNestedAgentsMd: Nested AGENTS.md files are off by default (chat.useNestedAgentsMdFiles).
copilot.$rules: An applyTo rule does not load when the agent reads a matching file. Tested 2026-10-21 with VS Code 1.142.0 and @github/copilot 1.0.95: before editing a matching file, the model read the applyTo file and the folder's AGENTS.md itself, from the instruction list Copilot puts into its prompt (documentation/agent-setup.md, 'When app rules load').
copilot.$pointerFile: Copilot reads AGENTS.md by itself, but not when chat.useAgentsMdFile is off; this file points it there either way.
copilot.$personal: Checked 2026-10-12 against https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/agent-skills and https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/mcp-servers. Which one wins for the same name, a personal skill or server against the project's, is not documented.

mcp.$why: The docs name the user mcp.json (command 'MCP: Open User Configuration') but give no Windows path; Code/User/mcp.json under %APPDATA% is the usual place for VS Code's user profile and is not confirmed.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.$skillLinks: Not tested (Cursor is not installed on the test machine). Copied, because Cursor's forum reports skills behind links not being found after a restart. Pending probe: Cursor's docs list .agents/skills as a folder it reads; if confirmed, this copy can go (documentation/agent-setup.md, 'How skills are found').
cursor.$disableModelInvocation: Not tested (Cursor is not installed on the test machine). Documented as honoured (https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills: such a skill 'is only included when explicitly invoked via /skill-name'). A forum report (Cursor 3.12.17, opened 2026-07-28; https://forum.cursor.com/t/disable-model-invocation-true-ignored-in-agents-skills/166846) said it is ignored for a skill in .agents/skills but honoured in .cursor/skills; on 2026-08-03 the reporter could not reproduce it in an empty repository, and the thread has no answer from Cursor. Cursor also reads .claude/skills, so with the Claude Code or Antigravity layout present it finds a project skill more than once.
cursor.$resolvesImports: Not tested (Cursor is not installed on the test machine): Cursor's documentation describes AGENTS.md as plain Markdown without imports.
cursor.$personal: Checked 2026-10-12 against https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills and https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp. Besides its own folders, Cursor reads ~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills for compatibility. Which one wins for the same name, a personal skill or server against the project's, is not documented.
